title: Gravity
subtitle: Same seed, same hardware, four gravity levels
description: The EMCS centrifuge sets gravity from zero to Earth-normal. Partial gravity changes how fast the root turns toward gravity, not where it ends up; in sealed dark hardware, zero gravity leaves the seedling with no up or down.

scenes.title: Gravity
lines: One seed model, four gravity levels, the same hardware.
The EMCS centrifuge on the International Space Station sets gravity from zero to Earth-normal, so everything else stays fixed.

scenes.title: EMCS centrifuge: zero, lunar, Mars and Earth gravity

captions.text: Endosperm rupture: {A.endosperm_rupture_h|1} h at zero gravity, {D.endosperm_rupture_h|1} h at Earth gravity. The gap comes from how water wets the blotter, an assumed input.
Once the root is out, it turns toward gravity, except at zero gravity, where it keeps growing straight.
At {A.t@48|0} h the root has turned {B.root_angle_deg@48-180|0}° at lunar gravity, {C.root_angle_deg@48-180|0}° at Mars gravity and {D.root_angle_deg@48-180|0}° at Earth gravity.
Every level above zero ends with a vertical root ({B.root_angle_deg:end-180|0}° at lunar gravity): partial gravity changes how fast the root turns, not where it ends up.
The gravity response comes from a separate model of auxin redistribution in the root tip (virtual-root): a model output, not a measurement.

caveats: How water wets the substrate at low gravity is assumed, not measured.
The root's gravity response is scaled from a separate auxin-transport model.

scenes.title: Sealed and dark: BRIC-PDFU in orbit and on the ground

captions.text: The same sealed dish, in orbit and at Earth gravity. No light, no air exchange.
Rupture at {A.endosperm_rupture_h|1} h in orbit and {B.endosperm_rupture_h|1} h on the ground: again set by the assumed wetting of the substrate.
Without gravity or light the seedling has no up or down: the root and hypocotyl keep growing the way the embryo pointed in the seed.
On the ground the root has turned {B.root_angle_deg:end-180|0}°; in orbit, {A.root_angle_deg:end-180|0}°.

caveats: How water wets the substrate at low gravity is assumed, not measured.
